analytics-overview.title: Analytics
analytics-overview.description: Track every scan with detailed insights while staying privacy-compliant.

sections.title: Privacy and compliance
sections.content: QRise is built with privacy-first principles. We use non-invasive fingerprinting to track unique scans without storing PII (Personally Identifiable Information). Our analytics are GDPR and CCPA compliant by default.

sections.title: Bot filtering
sections.content: We automatically filter out scans from known bots, spiders, and search engine crawlers. This ensures your analytics represent real human engagement.

endpoint.title: Create a QR code
endpoint.description: Creates a new QR code. For Dynamic QRs the short redirect code is generated automatically. For password-protected QRs supply the raw password — it will be hashed server-side.
notes: Plan limits apply: Free accounts can create up to 5 QR codes. Pro allows unlimited.
Password QRs require the password field and are always dynamic.

bodyParams.name: name
bodyParams.description: Display name for this QR code. Max 200 chars.

bodyParams.name: target_url
bodyParams.description: The destination URL. Required for url, smart_routing, and password types. Must begin with https:// or http://.

bodyParams.name: is_dynamic
bodyParams.description: When true, the QR encodes a short redirect that can be updated without reprinting. Default: true.

bodyParams.name: password
bodyParams.description: Required when type is password. Raw string — hashed server-side. Never stored in plaintext.

bodyParams.name: design
bodyParams.description: Design configuration. See Design object below.

bodyParams.name: design.dot_color
bodyParams.description: Hex color for QR dots. Default: #000000.

bodyParams.name: design.background_color
bodyParams.description: Hex color for QR background. Default: #ffffff.

bodyParams.name: design.error_correction
bodyParams.description: Error correction level. Higher levels allow larger logos but reduce data density.

responseSchema.name: short_code
responseSchema.description: 8-character URL-safe redirect code. Null for static QRs.

responseSchema.name: redirect_url
responseSchema.description: Full scannable URL encoded in the QR (e.g. https://r.qrise.io/abc12345). Null for static QRs.

responseSchema.name: is_dynamic
responseSchema.description: Whether this QR uses a redirect.

responseSchema.name: is_active
responseSchema.description: Whether this QR is currently scannable.

examples.python:
import requests
response = requests.post('https://api.qrise.io/qr',
    headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_API_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
    json={'name': 'Summer sale campaign', 'type': 'url', 'target_url': 'https://yourstore.com/summer-sale', 'is_dynamic': True})
qr = response.json()
print(qr['redirect_url'])
examples.curl: curl -X POST https://api.qrise.io/qr -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name": "Summer sale campaign", "type": "url", "target_url": "https://yourstore.com/summer-sale", "is_dynamic": true}'

custom-types-field-schema.title: Custom Types — Field Schema
custom-types-field-schema.description: Define structured data fields for your custom QR types using JSON Schema Draft-07.

sections.title: Key principles
sections.content: The fields_schema field follows JSON Schema Draft-07. Only object schemas with properties are supported — primitives at the root level are rejected.
items: Root must have type: 'object'
Define fields via properties object
Use required[] array to enforce mandatory fields
Supported property types: string, number, boolean, array, object
Use enum for fixed choices
Maximum depth: 3 levels (object-in-object-in-object)

sections.title: Example hospital wristband
sections.content: A typical use case: patient identification with ward and blood type as controlled vocabularies.

sections.title: Validation at creation
sections.content: The API validates your schema on creation:
items: Must be valid JSON (of course)
$schema must be omitted or set to Draft-07
No $ref — inline schemas only
No circular references
Maximum size: 5 KB

sections.title: Schema updates
sections.content: When you update a type's schema via PATCH /types/:slug, the version number increments. Existing QR codes keep the schema version they were created with — only new QRs use the updated schema. This ensures backward compatibility.

custom-types-marketplace.title: Custom Types — Marketplace
custom-types-marketplace.description: Share your custom QR types with the QRise community or discover types built by others.

sections.title: What is the marketplace?
sections.content: The marketplace is a curated collection of public custom types that have been verified by the QRise admin team. It's a place to discover useful QR type definitions or share your own with the world.
items: Only is_public=true AND is_verified=true types appear
Admin approval required (typically 3 business days)
Shows creator username, scan count, QR count
Categories: healthcare, hospitality, retail, events, logistics, other

sections.title: Submitting your type
sections.content: Before submitting, ensure your type meets these requirements:
items: Type must be is_public=true with a description and icon_url
Resolver must be active and tested (use the Test Resolver button first)
Fields schema must be well-documented and appropriate for general use
You can have maximum 3 pending submissions at a time

sections.title: Review process
sections.content: The QRise admin team reviews each submission for quality, appropriateness, and completeness. You'll receive email notification when your submission is approved or rejected (with feedback).
items: Review time: 1–3 business days
We check schema validity, naming clarity, and example use cases
Rejection includes notes for improvement
Approved types get a Verified badge and enter the marketplace

sections.title: Discovering types
sections.content: Browse the public marketplace without authentication. Filter by category, search by name/slug, sort by usage or recency. When you find a type you want to use, click 'Use this type' to create QRs of that type from your account.

custom-types-overview.title: Custom Types
custom-types-overview.description: Create custom QR code types with validation schemas and external resolver endpoints for dynamic content delivery.

sections.title: What are custom types?
sections.content: Custom types let you define structured data fields that a QR code carries. When scanned, the QR code triggers a resolver endpoint you control — enabling hospital wristbands, event tickets, product labels, and more.
items: Define arbitrary fields via JSON Schema (Draft-07)
Resolution happens at the edge via Cloudflare Worker
Resolver can return redirect, HTML, or JSON + template rendering
Patrons can submit public types to the marketplace
Plan limits apply: max_custom_types from plan_rate_limits

sections.title: Creating a type
sections.content: Use POST /types to register a new custom type with a globally-unique slug and valid JSON Schema. The schema defines all fields your QR codes will require when using this type.

sections.title: Field schema
sections.content: The fields_schema must be a valid JSON Schema object. Supported types: string, number, boolean, array, object. Use enum for fixed choices and required to enforce mandatory fields.

sections.title: Resolver protocol
sections.content: The resolver is your HTTPS endpoint that receives scan context and returns how the user should be routed. QRise signs every request with HMAC-SHA256 and enforces a configurable timeout.

sections.title: Templates
sections.content: When your resolver returns type=json, you can specify a Mustache template slug to render the data into HTML at the edge. QRise fetches and renders the template, protecting you from XSS.

sections.title: Marketplace
sections.content: Make your custom type public and submit it to the marketplace for other QRise users to discover. Admin review required — typically 3 business days.

custom-types-register.title: Custom Types — Register a Type
custom-types-register.description: Create a new custom QR type with a JSON Schema to define its data fields.

sections.title: Endpoint
sections.content: POST /v1/types

table.description: Unique lowercase slug, max 80 chars, hyphens only
Optional icon URL for marketplace listing
Whether this type is visible to other users

sections.title: Response
sections.content: Returns the created type with schema version starting at 1. Any future schema changes increment version — existing QRs retain their old payload structure.
items: id: UUID of type
slug, name, version
created_at timestamp

sections.title: Common errors
sections.content: 409 if max_custom_types limit reached. 422 if fields_schema is invalid JSON Schema. 409 if slug already exists.
items: 409 CONFLICT: Plan limit reached or slug taken
422 VALIDATION_ERROR: Invalid JSON Schema
403 FORBIDDEN: Insufficient types:write scope

custom-types-resolver-protocol.title: Custom Types — Resolver Protocol
custom-types-resolver-protocol.description: How QRise calls your external resolver endpoint with signed requests and handles responses.

sections.title: What is a resolver?
sections.content: When a custom type QR is scanned, QRise Cloudflare Worker makes a signed POST request to your configured resolver URL. Your server returns a response that determines what the scanner sees — a redirect, raw HTML, or structured data that gets template-rendered.

sections.title: Request from QRise
sections.content: Your resolver receives a POST with JSON body containing scan_context and the QR's custom payload.
items: Content-Type: application/json
Signature format: HMAC-SHA256(timestamp.body)
Timeout: configurable (default 3000ms, max from plan limits)
User-Agent: QRise-Resolver/1.0

sections.title: Valid response formats
sections.content: Your resolver must return JSON with a type field indicating how to handle the request.
items: { type: 'redirect', url: 'https://...' } → 302 redirect

{ type: 'html', html: '

...

' } → HTML displayed directly
{ type: 'json', data: {...}, template?: 'slug' } → Template renders data

sections.title: Security
sections.content: Always verify the X-QRise-Signature header using your secret. Reject requests with timestamps older than 5 minutes to prevent replay attacks. Verify that type matches your expected type slug.
items: Signature: HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp.body)
Reject old timestamps (>5 min)
Check X-QRise-Type matches your type
Respond within timeout_ms or fallback triggers

sections.title: Timeout & fallback
sections.content: If your resolver does not respond within timeout_ms (configurable per type), QRise will either redirect to fallback_url or render fallback_html. If neither is configured, users see an error page.
items: Default timeout: 3000 ms
Maximum: plan's max_resolver_timeout_ms
Plan limits: Enterprise up to 5000ms
On timeout: fallback_url → fallback_html → error page

link.text: View example resolver code (Node.js, Python, cURL) →

custom-types-templates.title: Custom Types — Templates
custom-types-templates.description: Create Mustache templates to render structured JSON data into HTML at the edge.

sections.title: What are templates?
sections.content: Templates let you separate presentation from resolver logic. Your resolver returns JSON data along with a template slug; QRise renders the Mustache template at the edge, shielding you from XSS.
items: Templates use Mustache syntax: {{variable}}
Available variables: all fields_schema properties + scan_context
Rendered server-side at Cloudflare edge
Up to 10 templates per type
One template can be set as default

sections.title: Available variables
sections.content: In your template HTML, you can access these top-level variables:
sections.code:
{{patient_id}}           ← field from fields_schema
{{ward}}                 ← another field
{{device_type}}          ← from scan_context
{{country}}              ← ISO country code
{{os}}                   ← operating system
{{language}}             ← BCP 47 language tag
items: Scan context fields: device_type, os, country, language, timestamp
Payload fields: whatever you defined in fields_schema
All values are automatically HTML-escaped

sections.title: Example hospital template
sections.content: A nurse-facing view showing patient details with conditional rendering:

sections.title: API endpoints
sections.content: Templates are managed via the types API:
items: GET /types/{slug}/templates — list all templates
POST /types/{slug}/templates — create (slug, name, template_html, is_default)
PATCH /types/{slug}/templates/:templateSlug — update HTML or default flag
DELETE /types/{slug}/templates/:templateSlug — delete

custom-types-test-resolver.title: Custom Types — Test Resolver
custom-types-test-resolver.description: Send test requests to your custom type resolver to validate connectivity and response format.

sections.title: Endpoint
sections.content: POST /v1/types/:slug/resolver/test

sections.title: Purpose
sections.content: The test endpoint sends a synthetic scan_context to your resolver without creating a real scan event. This is how you verify your resolver is correctly configured before going live.
items: No quota consumption (doesn't count against resolver_calls_per_month)
Does NOT create a resolver_calls log entry
Immediate response with status, latency, and parsed result
Includes signature verification check

sections.title: Request body
sections.content: Optionally provide your own scan_context for specific device/country testing. If omitted, a default context (mobile/US) is used.

table.description: HTTP status code returned by your resolver
Time from request to final byte
True if resolver timed out and fallback was used
Whether our signature matched your verification

errors.description: Standardized error responses help you debug issues quickly.

sections.title: Error format
sections.content: All errors are returned in a consistent JSON format:

forms-overview.title: Forms
forms-overview.description: Collect data from scanners using dynamic forms and webhooks.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: QRise allows you to attach a lead capture form to any dynamic QR code. When a user scans the QR, they are presented with a form before being redirected to the target URL.

sections.title: Supported field types
items: Email (validated)
Short text
Long text (paragraphs)
Select / Dropdown
Checkbox / Consent

sections.title: Data handling
sections.content: Form submissions can be retrieved via the API, exported to CSV, or sent in real-time to your CRM via webhooks.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: Create your first QR code in minutes.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: This guide will help you create your first dynamic QR code using the QRise API. You'll need an API key from your dashboard.

sections.title: 1. Create a QR code
sections.content: Send a POST request to /qr to create a dynamic URL QR:

sections.title: 2. Save the redirect URL
sections.content: The response will include a `redirect_url`. This is the URL that you should encode into your QR code image. You can also download the generated image directly from our API.

sections.title: 3. Track scans
sections.content: As soon as you scan the QR code, analytics will start populating in your dashboard and via the analytics API.

rate-limits.title: Rate Limits
rate-limits.description: API rate limits ensure stability and fair usage for todos los usuarios.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: QRise enforces rate limits on a per-API-key basis. If you exceed these limits, the API will respond with a 429 Too Many Requests error.

sections.title: Rate limit headers
sections.content: Every response includes headers to help you track your usage:
items: X-RateLimit-Limit: Total requests allowed per window
X-RateLimit-Remaining: Requests remaining in current window
X-RateLimit-Reset: Seconds until window resets

response-format.title: Response Format
response-format.description: All v1 API responses follow a consistent envelope structure for both success and error cases.

sections.title: Standard envelope
sections.content: Every response from the QRise API — including errors — is wrapped in a JSON envelope with a consistent shape.

sections.title: Success response
sections.content: Successful requests return ok: true with the actual data in the data field. The meta object contains pagination and usage information.

sections.title: Error response
sections.content: Failed requests return ok: false with an error object containing a machine-readable code, human-readable message, and optional details.

sections.title: Usage tracking in meta
sections.content: Every successful v1 response includes usage statistics in meta. This lets you monitor your quota consumption in real-time without making a separate /usage call.
items: calls_this_month: Your billable API calls this month
calls_limit: Your plan's monthly limit
resets_at: When the current period ends (UTC midnight on 1st of month)

sections.title: Rate limit headers
sections.content: In addition to the body envelope, every response includes rate limit headers:
sections.code:
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 67
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1714000000
X-RateLimit-Window: 60
X-QRise-Request-Id: req_uuid
X-QRise-Plan: pro

sections.title: Common error codes
sections.content: The error.code field is a stable identifier you can programmatically check for. Do not parse error.message — it may change.
items: BAD_REQUEST (400): Malformed JSON or invalid parameters
UNAUTHORIZED (401): Missing or invalid API key
FORBIDDEN (403): Valid key but insufficient scope
NOT_FOUND (404): Resource doesn't exist
VALIDATION_ERROR (422): Request body fails validation
RATE_LIMITED (429): Too many requests — check Retry-After header
INTERNAL_ERROR (500): QRise server error

sandbox.title: Sandbox Environment
sandbox.description: Test your integration safely using isolated sandbox data that never touches production.

sections.title: What is the sandbox?
sections.content: The sandbox environment provides complete isolation from your live production data. Sandbox API keys (qr_test_*) read and write to a separate database schema, ensuring test QRs, scans, and webhooks never pollute your production metrics or billing.

sections.title: Using the sandbox
sections.content: To use the sandbox, create an API key with the qr_test_ prefix (available from your dashboard). All requests made with a sandbox key are routed to the sandbox schema automatically.

sections.title: Complete isolation
sections.content: Sandbox data is stored in a separate PostgreSQL schema and cached separately in Redis. There is no risk of test data affecting production analytics, billing calculations, or rate limits. However, plan limits (like max_custom_types) are still enforced per environment.
items: Sandbox QRs are not visible in the production dashboard
Sandbox scans do not count toward analytics or billing
Sandbox API usage does not consume your paid quota
Sandbox webhooks fire to test endpoints only

sections.title: Switching between environments
sections.content: To switch from sandbox to live, simply use a qr_live_ key. The API behavior is identical; only the data routing differs. Your code does not need to change — swap the key and you're in production.

smart-routing-overview.title: Smart Routing
smart-routing-overview.description: Smart Routing allows you to redirect users to different destinations based on their device, location, time, or language.

sections.title: How it works
sections.content: When a user scans a Smart Routing QR code, QRise evaluates a list of rules from top to bottom. The first rule that matches the user's scan context (device, location, etc.) determines the destination. If no rules match, the user is sent to the default URL.

sections.title: Rule evaluation
items: Rules are evaluated in order of priority (lowest number first)
The first matching rule 'wins'
If multiple conditions exist in a rule, ALL must match (AND logic)
If no rule matches, the default destination is used

usage-alerts.title: Usage Alerts
usage-alerts.description: Configure Slack, Discord, or email notifications when your API usage reaches a threshold.

sections.title: What are usage alerts?
sections.content: Usage alerts proactively notify you when your consumption approaches plan limits. Set a threshold percentage (50–100%) and we'll send a message to your chosen channel before you hit overage charges.
items: Three channel types: Slack (Incoming Webhook), Discord (Webhook), Email
Threshold: 50%–100% (default 80%)
One alert per threshold per month (no spam)
Alert includes current usage, reset date, and upgrade link

sections.title: Slack alerts
sections.content: Create an Incoming Webhook in your Slack workspace (Apps → Incoming Webhooks). Copy the webhook URL and use it as the webhook_url parameter.
items: Go to slack.com/apps → search 'Incoming Webhooks'
Add to your workspace, pick a channel
Copy the webhook URL (starts with https://hooks.slack.com/services/)
Create alert with channel_type='slack'

sections.title: Discord alerts
sections.content: Create a Discord Webhook in your server: Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Create Webhook. Copy the URL.
items: Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks
Choose channel and create webhook
Copy the webhook URL
Create alert with channel_type='discord'

sections.title: Email alerts
sections.content: Provide any email address. Notifications are sent from alerts@qrise.io. Add this to your contacts to avoid spam filtering.
items: Simple: just provide an email address
Emails come from alerts@qrise.io
Whitelist this address to ensure delivery

sections.title: Testing and management
sections.content: Each alert channel has a test button in the dashboard and a POST /usage/alerts/:id/test endpoint to verify delivery before relying on it. You can also list, update, or delete alerts via the API.
items: POST /usage/alerts/:id/test sends a test notification
DELETE /usage/alerts/:id removes the channel
GET /usage/alerts lists all configured channels

usage.title: Usage & Billing
usage.description: Track your API consumption, monitor limits, and understand billing metrics.

sections.title: Usage endpoint
sections.content: The /usage endpoint returns detailed consumption data for the current or any historical month. All usage is tracked automatically on every API call.

sections.title: Usage history
sections.content: View 12 months of historical usage snapshots to identify trends and plan capacity.

sections.title: Usage export
sections.content: Download a CSV of all API events for a given month for internal reconciliation or audit purposes.

sections.title: Usage alerts
sections.content: You can create alert channels to notify you via Slack, Discord, or email when usage crosses a threshold (50–100%). Alerts are sent once per threshold crossing per month to avoid noise.

webhooks-filters.title: Webhooks — Event Filters
webhooks-filters.description: Reduce webhook noise by filtering which specific QRs or events trigger notifications.

sections.title: Why filter?
sections.content: Not every webhook subscriber needs every event. Filters let you narrow the scope so you only receive relevant events, reducing unnecessary HTTP requests and processing.
items: Filter qr.scanned to specific QR IDs only
Filter qr.updated to URL-change-only events
Filter form.submission to specific forms
Filter usage.threshold_reached to your chosen percentage

sections.title: Filter structure
sections.content: The filter_config field on webhook creation/update is a JSON object where keys are event types and values are filter criteria.
items: Event-specific keys: qr.scanned, qr.updated, form.submission, usage.threshold_reached
Null or empty filter_config = receive ALL events of subscribed types
Multiple filters stack (AND logic)

sections.title: qr.scanned filter
sections.content: Limit scans to a specific set of QR codes. Useful when you only care about high-value QRs. The qr_ids array accepts up to 100 UUIDs per webhook.

sections.title: qr.updated filter
sections.content: Receive updates only when the target_url changes (not when name or design changes). Useful for redirect monitoring.

sections.title: usage.threshold_reached filter
sections.content: By default the threshold_reached event fires at 80%. Override per-webhook with min_pct (50–100).

webhooks-overview.title: Webhooks
webhooks-overview.description: Receive real-time notifications when events happen in your QRise account.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Webhooks allow your application to receive and react to events as they happen. QRise sends a POST request with a JSON payload to your configured endpoint.

sections.title: Retries
sections.content: If your server responds with anything other than 2xx, or times out (10s), QRise will retry delivery with exponential backoff up to 5 times over 12 hours.

webhooks-replay.title: Replay deliveries
webhooks-replay.description: Recover from delivery failures by re-sending past webhook events.

sections.title: When to replay
sections.content: If a webhook delivery fails (your endpoint returned non-2xx or timed out), you can replay it. This creates a new delivery attempt with the same payload and retry schedule. The original delivery record remains for audit.
items: Replay only failed or pending deliveries
Creates a new delivery with fresh retry clock
Original record preserved unchanged
Useful after temporary outage or bug fix

sections.title: List deliveries to find the ID
sections.content: Before replaying, you need the delivery ID. List deliveries for a webhook to find the failed one.

sections.title: Replay endpoint
sections.content: POST to the replay URL with the delivery ID in the path.
items: Returns: { new_delivery_id: uuid, status: 'pending' }
New delivery enters the retry queue immediately
No request body required

webhooks-test-replay.title: Webhooks — Test & Replay
webhooks-test-replay.description: Test your webhook integrations and replay failed deliveries.

sections.title: Testing webhooks
sections.content: The /webhooks/{id}/test endpoint sends a synthetic event immediately to your webhook URL. Use this to verify connectivity and signature validation during setup.
items: Method: POST /webhooks/{id}/test
Optional body: { event: 'qr.created' } — defaults to qr.created
Bypasses retry queue — delivered synchronously
Response includes delivered status, status_code, latency_ms, and the signature that was sent
Does NOT count against any quota

sections.title: Replaying deliveries
sections.content: If a webhook delivery failed (e.g., your endpoint was down), you can replay it from the delivery log. Replay creates a new delivery record with the same payload and retry schedule.
items: Method: POST /webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/replay
Original delivery record is preserved for audit
New delivery gets its own retry schedule
Useful for recovering from temporary outages

sections.title: Inspecting deliveries
sections.content: GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries returns a paginated list of all delivery attempts with status, response code, latency, and timestamp. Filter by status (pending, delivered, failed, retrying, abandoned) or event type.
items: Status pending: queued, not yet sent
Status delivered: endpoint returned 2xx
Status failed: non-2xx response or network error
Status retrying: will retry per schedule
Status abandoned: all 6 attempts exhausted

webhooks-test.title: Test webhook
webhooks-test.description: Send a test event to your webhook endpoint to verify connectivity and signature validation.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.content: Use the test endpoint to confirm your webhook URL is reachable and that you can correctly verify signatures. This sends a synthetic event immediately, bypassing the retry queue.
items: Immediate synchronous delivery
Does not count against any quota
Returns detailed result: delivered status, HTTP status, latency, and signature sent
Ideal for testing during initial setup

sections.title: Request
sections.content: POST /webhooks/{id}/test with optional event type in body.
sections.code:
POST https://api.qrise.io/webhooks/{id}/test

{ "event": "qr.created" }  // optional, defaults to qr.created

sections.title: Response
sections.content: Returns immediate delivery result:
items: delivered: boolean — true if your endpoint returned 2xx
status_code: number — HTTP status your endpoint returned
latency_ms: number — time from POST to final byte
response_body: string — truncated response (max 1 KB)
signature_sent: string — the X-QRise-Signature header value (for debugging)

webhooks-verify.title: Webhooks — Verify Signatures
webhooks-verify.description: Learn how to verify webhook signatures to ensure events are authentic and not tampered with.

sections.title: How signing works
sections.content: Every webhook delivery from QRise includes an X-QRise-Signature header. This is an HMAC-SHA256 signature of timestamp.request-body using your webhook secret. Verifying this signature ensures the request truly came from QRise and was not altered in transit.
items: Signature format: t=timestamp,v1=hmac
HMAC key: your webhook secret (shown once on creation)
Payload: raw request body as string (not parsed JSON)
Timestamp tolerance: 5 minutes (reject older requests)
Use timing-safe comparison to prevent timing attacks

sections.title: Verification algorithm
sections.content: Implement this logic on your webhook endpoint:
sections.code:
1. Extract header: 'X-QRise-Signature'
2. Split into parts: t=<timestamp>, v1=<hmac>
3. Check timestamp: reject if >5 minutes old
4. Compute your own HMAC: crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(timestamp + '.' + body).digest('hex')
5. Compare using timing-safe-equal
6. If equal → process event; else → return 401
